# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I only have one row of the manual, showing blue→yellow. I can't speak—only gesture to Deaf, and only Blind can act. I have no way to send anything to Blind directly; it must relay through Deaf and Blind's own turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf). Since Blind goes before Deaf, I need to get info to Deaf first, but Deaf can't act either. Actually the wire cut is Blind's action, so the info needs to reach Blind. I can't speak to Blind, and gestures only reach Deaf (who can see). So I must pass through Deaf somehow — but Deaf goes after Blind in turn order this round, so anything I gesture now reaches Deaf only at the point Deaf can send info to Blind next round.

I need an encoding: gesture a color+wire pair to Deaf using the alphabet, so Deaf can later relate it (combined with what Deaf sees on the bomb) to Blind via speech... wait, Deaf cannot speak either? Let me check - only Mute and Blind are restricted from speaking. Deaf can speak. So Deaf can hear nothing but CAN speak. Good - Deaf speaks to Blind.

So my job: gesture the manual info to Deaf in a way Deaf can decode, Deaf matches with the color they see, then Deaf tells Blind (via speech) which wire to cut.

I'll establish a gesture code for colors and wire names now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ☝]

Deaf gestured back the same symbols I sent — likely just mirroring/acknowledging receipt, not meaningful content yet since Deaf doesn't know my code. I need an actual plan: establish a simple gesture alphabet mapping specific symbols to colors and wire-colors, one pairing per round since only one gesture-message truly lands before Deaf's own turn each round (Mute→Blind→Deaf order, my gestures reach Deaf same round, but Deaf can't respond meaningfully back to me with new info since Deaf doesn't know the code yet either).

Better approach: I only have ONE row of the manual so far: blue→yellow. I should just teach Deaf a direct code: gesture 👍 = "blue", ☝ = "yellow", and pair them to mean "if you see blue, tell Blind to cut yellow". Since Deaf can't hear me confirm, I'll just define it via repetition and let context build. Let me send a clear single unambiguous pairing this turn.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf is mirroring back single symbols, likely just echoing to confirm reception since Deaf has no other way to communicate with me (Deaf can't speak to me in a way I'd hear — wait, actually Deaf CAN speak, but I can't hear). So Deaf's only channel to me is gesture, but Deaf cannot see gestures made *to* them from me and reciprocate content — Deaf is only echoing back what makes sense as acknowledgment.

I realize I'm overcomplicating. My real job: get "blue→yellow" info to Deaf in a way Deaf can act on with Blind. Deaf sees the bomb's actual light color. Deaf needs to know: "when the light is blue, the wire to cut is yellow." I should encode both color-names using gestures, consistently, so Deaf can build a private dictionary from repetition across rounds (since the manual table may grow with more rows over time, each associated with a distinct gesture pair).

Let me assign: 👍 = blue (light), ☝ = yellow (wire). I've sent this pairing twice now. Deaf's echo of 👍 alone this turn might mean "confirmed: 👍=blue" or could be Deaf asking "what does 👍 mean?" Since Deaf cannot ask questions via words to me, I'll just proceed assuming reception and reinforce with a combined single-turn message, since I can send multiple gestures in one call now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Deaf is now sending back the pair in reverse order [☝ 👍], compared to my [👍 ☝]. This looks like intentional feedback — Deaf might be testing whether order matters, or signaling "I see two symbols, but I'm not sure which is light-color and which is wire-color, please clarify direction."

I need to fix an unambiguous convention: first symbol = light color seen, second = wire to cut. Let me be very deliberate and use distinct, unlikely-to-be-confused symbols, and repeat the exact same order every time so Deaf can lock in the mapping. I'll also try a slightly different tactic: send them one at a time labeled by position via repetition, reinforcing 👍 always first (=blue/light) and ☝ always second (=yellow/wire).

Since Deaf can also speak to Blind, and Blind needs to know "cut yellow when blue," ultimately Deaf must translate my gesture-code into their own words to Blind. Deaf doesn't know color names as words necessarily map correctly - actually Deaf sees actual colors on the bomb directly, so Deaf already knows "blue" and "yellow" as concepts from sight. My gestures just need to indicate "manual says: this concept A maps to concept B" — Deaf can then match A to what they see.

Simplest: I'll use 👍 to consistently mean "the color/situation you currently see" placeholder is unnecessary — better, let me just commit to: 👍=blue, ☝=yellow, and send them in fixed order every round, ignoring Deaf's echo (which may just be an artifact/uncontrollable mirroring, not real feedback since Deaf might not even choose what to echo intentionally in this exercise).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝ "])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here: I need the wire-cutting rule from the manual. Please gesture the wire position to cut, or a code Deaf can relay to me as numbers.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Blind can hear me? No — I cannot speak, but wait, Blind's message arrived as text to me, meaning Blind spoke and I "heard" it as text in this transcript. Let me reconsider the channel rules: Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? The rules don't say Mute is deaf — only "Deaf" monkey cannot hear. So Mute CAN hear speech! That changes everything.

So Blind spoke (Blind can speak, just can't see or touch... wait Blind CAN touch, just can't see). Blind spoke to me asking for the rule. I can hear Blind's speech since I'm not deaf. But I cannot speak back to Blind directly. I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives gestures. So I still need Deaf as the relay to Blind.

Deaf keeps echoing back [☝ 👍] — reversed order from what I send. This might just be a lack of ability to distinguish/reproduce order, or Deaf is genuinely relaying "I see these two gesture-blanks were sent to me but in this order" — but wait, Deaf isn't blind, Deaf CAN see gestures fully (not blanks). So Deaf really does see 👍 then ☝, and Deaf's echo back of [☝ 👍] must be intentional - perhaps Deaf is telling me the actual bomb light color using MY code, matching by symbol not position: Deaf sees the light is currently showing something, and doesn't have "blue" yet since only one manual row exists (blue). Maybe Deaf is asking "which is which" by flipping to test.

Given Blind now explicitly asks me to gesture wire position "as numbers" via Deaf relay - but I can't gesture to Blind, only Deaf can relay by speaking. I need to instruct Deaf (via gesture) to tell Blind "cut yellow if you see blue light." Since gestures can't carry words directly readable by Deaf unless Deaf assigns meaning, I'll try using a number-like gesture sequence representing wire position instead, per Blind's request — but I don't know wire positions, only colors.

I'll clarify roles: tell Deaf (via consistent gesture code) that this is a color-to-color mapping, and trust Deaf to verbally relay the actual color name (blue/yellow) to Blind, since Deaf can speak and knows color words from sight.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```
